name: Sonnet growth at a reasonable price
strategy: Round 3: momentum/regime rotation narrowed to the legs that are actually still trending -- financials (JPM) and biotech (XBI) breakouts, a trimmed profit-take in healthcare (ELV), a continued energy uptrend (CVX) -- funded by exiting names whose price action stalled or broke down (UNP, V, PG, IJR), plus a new short in MSTR to fade the cracking Bitcoin blow-off top, with cash raised to 39% amid the newly hawkish rate regime.
reassessment_note: Friday's August jobs report (nonfarm payrolls +162k vs a ~31k trailing 12-month average, unemployment flat at 4.1%) triggered a hawkish repricing -- 'rate-hike jitters' per the tape, Treasury yields up, stocks down Thursday/Friday -- and Bitcoin broke back below $80k with ETF inflows reportedly collapsing 76% in a day after a three-week winning streak. That is exactly the confirmed-breakout / blow-off-top-reversal setup this book is mandated to trade on price action rather than valuation. I kept and sized up the two legs still showing a live trend in the new regime: JPM (banks are a direct beneficiary of a higher-for-longer rate path) and XBI (biotech breakout thesis intact, stop kept). I trimmed ELV after its ~37% run once 'valuation gap' commentary started circulating in this week's coverage -- still in the trend but sizing down into strength. I cut UNP (-6.10% on the leg, no breakout, Southern-merger overhang with no resolution catalyst), V (-1.92%, no confirmed trend either direction), PG (-0.11%, dead flat -- a staple that never fit a price-action mandate to begin with) and IJR (-0.97%, small caps facing the same rate-hike headwind as the Round 2 book's IWM sleeve) since none of them show the kind of confirmed signal this strategy requires to hold a position. New: a MSTR short to directly fade the crypto blow-off top the tape just confirmed (BTC below $80k on the hot jobs print, ETF inflows drying up) -- MSTR is the highest-beta, most liquid way to express that specific reversal call. Cash raised to 39% because the regime just shifted and roughly half the prior book no longer shows a signal worth holding through a repricing.

positions.thesis: Confirmed uptrend that got stronger, not weaker, on this week's hawkish jobs surprise: a higher-for-longer rate path is a direct tailwind for bank net interest margins, and JPM's relative strength on a day the broad market fell ('rate-hike jitters') is exactly the kind of regime-confirming price action this mandate trades on. Sized up from 13% to 16%.

Still in a confirmed uptrend (up ~37% on the broader run per this week's coverage) and the managed-care group got a supportive credit-rating-affirmation headline, but 'valuation gap' commentary is now circulating, which is the kind of chatter that precedes a breakout losing steam. Trimming from 12% to 10% to lock in some of the trend while staying long it.

Continues its uptrend (+2.71% on the leg) and showed relative strength into this week's broad-market wobble, consistent with an energy complex that benefits from a higher-for-longer/inflation-surprise regime. Sized up from 8% to 12% on confirmed relative strength.

Core biotech-breakout expression of the mandate; price action remains within the trend (only -0.22% on the leg) with no stop breach. Sizing up from 12% to 15% since this is one of only two clean uptrends left in the book after this week's regime shift, and keeping the protective stop.

New leg to fade a confirmed blow-off-top reversal in crypto, squarely in the mandate's 'fade blow-off-top reversals in crypto' bucket. This week Bitcoin broke back below $80k on the hot jobs print after a three-week rally, and Bitcoin ETF inflows reportedly collapsed 76% in a single day -- a classic exhaustion signal. MSTR, a heavily levered Bitcoin proxy, is the highest-beta way to press that reversal. Sized at 8% with a 15% stop given MSTR's extreme volatility.
